subject: The two Beneteau First marks now differ only in their digits
request: docs/post-mvp/0_3_0_OWNER_BRIEF.md section 1.6, with docs/post-mvp/brief-0.3.0/first-marks-reference.png as the specification
ownerInstruction: rendili uguali in tutto e per tutto uno all'altro tranne per il numero. Usa come base quello di sotto, ma mettendo i numeri con dimensione di quello di sopra, allineati a destra verticalmente con la scritta FIRST.
why: first-27.png was the 25.7 artwork with the .7 glyph run cleared, which is why its number was small and sat nowhere in particular. The 2026-09-20 plan entry recorded this as an open product call: redraw the artwork or fall back to the written mark.
method: first-27.png is the base for both: its canvas, seahorse plate and FIRST wordmark are used unchanged, and the area between the plate and the wordmark is cleared.

The numerals are lifted from first-25-7.png at their native 14 px height, so they are the same typeface at the same size in both marks. 27 is composed from that mark's own 2 and 7 glyph runs, joined with the 6 px gap the source uses between 2 and 5.
Each numeral run is placed with its right edge on column 101, which is the last column of the FIRST wordmark.
The numerals' baseline is left where the base already had it, bottom row 36, because only the size and the horizontal alignment were asked to change.

pixelDifferenceBetweenTheTwoFiles.meaning: Every differing pixel lies inside the digit run. The plate, the wordmark, the canvas and the shared trailing 7 are byte-identical, which is the owner's 'uguali in tutto e per tutto tranne per il numero' stated as a measurement.

verified: npm run verify:e2e -- tests/e2e/ug1-boat-mark-fit.spec.ts --project=pixel-7-chrome passed: it builds a fleet of all seven canonical types and measures each image against its 36x88 slot, and it measures the card height.
noted: The 27 mark now carries 32 px of empty space between the plate and its digits, against 6 px on the 25.7 mark, because both are right-aligned to the wordmark and 27 is the shorter run. That is what right-alignment means here and it is what the reference image shows.
